A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable, and relocated or renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original race-probe AUROCs, steering experiments, vignette-generation results and clinical bias-mitigation evaluations, including multilayer ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a qualitative GPT-OSS-20B latent-activation analysis in Appendix B.1 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: Probe-based latent identification, clinical reinterpretation, steering and zero-ablation procedures are retained. The additional model analysis and effect-score correction do not establish a changed intervention algorithm.

E1.justification: MIMIC-III notes, MIMIC-IV-derived hospital courses and Q-Pain remain the data sources, with the same clinical tasks. GPT-OSS-20B adds a model configuration within clinical-note analysis. Renaming risk prediction as diagnosis evidence does not introduce a new task.

E2.justification: The same unmodified-model and anti-bias-prompting comparisons are retained for vignette generation and clinical tasks, alongside the white-latent steering control. GPT-OSS-20B is an additional analysis subject, not a competing mitigation baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds evaluation using GPT-OSS-20B and its middle-layer SAE. Equation 2 reverses the reported effect-score convention, and Appendix D.1 changes the displayed Q-Pain prompts from 'Caucasian' to 'White'. These reporting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 and Figure 6 add a qualitative check of whether racial and stigmatizing latent associations also occur in GPT-OSS-20B. Existing steering-factor sensitivity and five-layer ablation analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The paired t-tests, p < 0.05 reporting and Figure 3 error bars are retained. Neither version supplies additional repeated-run counts, seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds GPT-OSS-20B activation examples involving Black identity, incarceration, cocaine and jail. Existing Gemma results remain unchanged: AUROCs are 0.63 and 0.72, and the steering rates, vignette ratios, clinical bias results and FLDD values are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes the summed effect from ablated-minus-original to original-minus-ablated. This corrects the mathematical definition's sign relative to the stated interpretation of positive effects. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding discussion retain the same central contributions: revealing racial associations, demonstrating unfaithful CoT explanations through steering, and finding weaker mitigation effects in realistic clinical tasks. The new GPT-OSS examples supplement these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains stronger activation on 'American' through last-token representations, interprets the GPT-OSS examples as generalization beyond Gemma, and more explicitly rejects population-prevalence reasoning for diagnosis evidence. The entanglement explanation and original limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future-code-release promise with a repository address and adds HuggingFace/NNsight, two NVIDIA H200 GPUs and the GPT-OSS SAE checkpoint. It also newly specifies male patients for cocaine-abuse sampling; unchanged dataset statistics do not establish a changed cohort.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Meng et al. on factual representations, Fiotto-Kaufman et al. on NNsight, and the GPT-OSS model card. The related-work discussion and positioning of the central contribution remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited prose and terminology edits, consolidates the summary and conclusions into Discussion before Related Work, and adds Ethics, Reproducibility and LLM-use sections. The publication header and acknowledgements change, while most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the GPT-OSS activation figure and expands Figure 1's caption. Tables 2 and 3 exchange numbering and placement, while the retained perplexity plot becomes Figure 7 beside Table 9. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the sign inconsistency in Equation 2, improves reproducibility documentation and adds limited evidence beyond Gemma. These strengthen clarity and support without changing the main quantitative conclusions. The gain is modest: the GPT-OSS evidence is qualitative, and the retained limitation claiming analysis only of Gemma is not reconciled with that addition.
